documents.title: Operational Plan for Weather Modification Project — Western Kansas Weather Modification 2014
documents.summary: Continuation of the program run during growing seasons 1975–2013; 3 counties in 2014. Operations April 16–September 15, 2014. Methods: dry ice injected into clouds, silver iodide vaporized into cloud-base updrafts (3% solution in wing-tip generators, and pyrotechnics), hygroscopic pyrotechnic flares. Aircraft: two single-engine Piper Comanche (cloud base) and a twin-engine Piper Cheyenne (cloud top), owned by WKGMD #1. Field headquarters at Kearny County Airport, Lakin. Expected area of influence about 10 miles upwind and 25 miles downwind of the target counties.

documents.title: 15 CFR Part 908 — Maintaining Records and Submitting Reports on Weather Modification Activities
documents.summary: Anyone doing weather modification in the U.S. must report to NOAA at least 10 days before starting, and file activity reports. NOAA collects reports but does not regulate the activity.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.summary: Kansas licenses and permits weather modification under the Kansas Weather Modification Act (K.S.A. 82a-1401 et seq., 1974), administered by the Kansas Water Office / Kansas Water Authority. Two 2026 bills to ban it died. One program is documented: the Western Kansas Weather Modification Program (HISTORICAL — last NOAA report 2016; operator says suspended).

records.operator: Western Kansas Groundwater Management District No. 1 (WKGMD #1)
records.targetArea: Groups of counties in southwest and west-central Kansas, varying by year (2016 NOAA report: Scott and Lane counties). Map in the 2014 operational plan.
records.affectedArea: Per 2014 operational plan: about 10 miles upwind and 25 miles downwind of the target counties.
records.sourceAgency: NOAA Central Library (reports filed under 15 CFR 908)
records.notes: The operator's website says the program has been suspended for funding reasons (no date given). No NOAA report after the 2016 season appears in the 2000–2025 dataset. Its operating area is in western Kansas, roughly 350–370 miles west of Kansas City — far outside the KC area. Kansas license and permit numbers were not found in any online source; the Kansas Water Office holds those records.
